newsitem.title: POLAND: Saint-Gobain opens Polish glass plant.
newsitem.headline: Saint-Gobain opens Polish glass plant.

text.p: French glass maker Cie de Saint-Gobain opened on Thursday a 180 million German mark state-of-the-art glass mill in the southern Polish town of Strzemieszyce after 20 months of construction work.

"60 million marks for the investment came from a consortium of Polish banks, 40 million from German and French banks and 80 million from Saint-Gobain's own funds," the plant's president Guy Rolli told a news conference.

The Polfloat plant, employing 280 people, will produce 15 million square metres of float glass annually, Rolli said. Half of its production would be exported to central European countries, Germany, Greece and Scandinavia.

Rolli also said Saint-Gobain planned to invest a further 500 million marks in Poland by the end of the century in developing, among other ventures, the production of laminated and specially hardened glass for the automotive industry.
